claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi naturally forms a protective passive oxide film under ambient conditions.
The tribo-corrosion response of AlCoCrFeNi is governed by repeated passive-film rupture and reformation.
Sliding abrasion mechanically removes sections of the protective passive film.
Chloride destabilizes the passive film on AlCoCrFeNi.
The combination of sliding and chloride exposure prevents rapid and complete repassivation.
In chloride solution, exposed alloy is attacked by the electrolyte before the passive film can fully regenerate.
Film rupture followed by electrolyte attack creates a feedback loop that amplifies corrosion.
Film rupture followed by electrolyte attack creates a feedback loop that amplifies wear.
An inert lubricant minimizes chemical dissolution during sliding.
The passive film reforms quickly in the inert environment.
Wear is the predominant degradation mechanism in the inert-lubricant baseline.
Sliding in 3.5% NaCl will produce significantly greater total degradation than sliding under matched conditions in an inert lubricant.
Sliding in 3.5% NaCl will increase wear volume relative to the inert-lubricant baseline.
Sliding in 3.5% NaCl will produce deeper or more widespread corrosion pits than the inert-lubricant baseline.
The predicted synergy should occur when the passive film is sensitive to both chloride attack and mechanical stress.
Very rapid intrinsic repassivation may suppress the predicted synergistic degradation.
Mechanical loads too low to disrupt the film extensively may suppress the predicted synergistic degradation.
